tb21_profile.skill: Recognise credential formats (AWS key id/secret, ghp_, hf_) anywhere in a repository including git history, replace each with a consistent placeholder, and leave every uncontaminated file byte-identical
tb21_profile.domain: Git internals and secret hygiene: grep/sed over a checkout, git log/history rewriting, credential formats
tb21_profile.task_form: recover/repair: surgical sanitisation of an existing repo under a strict do-no-collateral-damage constraint

verifier_notes: I disagree with the FREE grade on security_20260510_062946_007 (CalibForge). Read its tests/test_outputs.py: it asserts specific real secret strings are ABSENT from named files, that specific <your-aws-access-key-id>-style placeholders are PRESENT, and that documented example keys and test fixtures are still intact - negative plus positive plus preservation assertions, not a file-exists suite. The heuristic scored it FREE because every assertion is of the form 'substring in content'. It is the single closest candidate to this TB2.1 task and I still kept it out of final_top10 because the hard rule is mechanical; the merge step should consider re-grading it. security_20260419_112101_007, tw_147333 and tw_361500 are also FREE and likewise ranked in per_source only. [fix-team 05, corrected-grader pass] The grader has since been corrected and work/verifier_strength.json now grades security_20260510_062946_007 `strong`, so the mechanical bar is gone and I have promoted it to rank 1, displacing task_000841_29b88124 (was rank 10, overall 3, grade unaffected, still in per_source - a single-file AKIA substitution that 062946_007 subsumes entirely). It goes above security_20260430_081156_007 because it is the only candidate that is this TB2.1 task rather than half of it: same repo-wide sanitisation, the same literal <your-aws-access-key-id> / <your-github-token> / <your-huggingface-token> placeholder wording the TB2.1 prompt uses, and the secrets must also be gone from `git log -p --all`, which 081156_007 (log files, no git) does not touch. One correction to my earlier reading, having gone back through tests/test_outputs.py line by line: I previously wrote that it asserts doc and fixture files are unmodified. It does not. AWS_EXAMPLE_ACCESS_KEY, TEST_FIXTURES and FILES_TO_PRESERVE are defined at the top of the file and then never referenced by any of the 11 tests - dead constants. So the positive half is verified hard (nine named high-entropy secrets must be absent from named files and from all of git history, and eight exact placeholder strings must be present), but the real-vs-fixture triage the instruction makes the point of the task is not checked at all, and a blanket sed over the whole tree passes. That is worth knowing downstream: it is the one axis on which it teaches less than TB2.1 asks, and it is why task_12998 (delete only the secret-bearing rows, leave clean rows byte-identical) keeps its slot at rank 10 despite an overall of 3 - it is the only entry left that verifies the do-no-collateral-damage constraint. security_20260419_112101_007 is also rehabilitated (now `strong`) but stays out on merit at overall 3: purging SSH keys from all branches and tags is already covered by ranks 3, 6 and 7.

notes: CalibForge is decisively the best pool for this task: it has a whole security/ family that is this task (log and repo sanitisation with angle-bracket placeholders, git-history credential purges, secret scanners, real-vs-fixture triage) and takes 5 of the final 10. Terminal-Lego adds two genuinely good ones (remove a file from git history; selectively delete only secret rows) plus solid recursive sed/in-place-edit mechanics the v1 pool only had incidentally. TMax is strong on both halves separately (AKIA redaction with pinned output; recovering secrets from git history) but never combines them. Recursive-Task-Synthesis actually has real secret.key history-rewrite tasks - unusually good for that corpus - but all `absent`, so I preferred the graded TerminalWorld twin tw_329715 in the final. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have nothing about secrets except stackprinter's censoring logic; their 10 are mostly git-library (dulwich/GitPython) internals scored honestly low on task_form.
